chunks: Ali, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Ibn Azina, from Bukeyr Bin Ayn, and Bureyd Bin Muawiya, from Abu Ja’far and Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) who said:

The one who buys a slave girl who has a husband for her, so her sale is her divorce. So, if the buyer so desires to, he effects separation between them, and if he so desires to he leaves them both upon their marriage.
ai.seo_question: What is the legal effect on a slave girl's marriage when she is sold?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi outlines the juristic principle that selling a female slave with an existing husband automatically effects her divorce (talaq), a ruling derived from the buyer's acquisition of her 'franchise' (ibrah) to keep or release her. It highlights the distinct status of slave-women in Shia fiqh, where the buyer holds the discretion to maintain the marital bond or dissolve it, reflecting the interplay between ownership and family law in classical Islamic jurisprudence.

en.hubeali:
Ali, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Ibn Azina, from Bukeyr Bin Ayn, and Bureyd Bin Muawiya, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> and Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> both having said:

‘The one who buys a slave girl who has a husband for her, so her sale is her divorce. So, if the buyer so desires to, he effects separation between them, and if he so desires to he leaves them both upon their marriage’.
